name: PaperFate Q500 rubric schema

special_codes.NA: Not applicable for this article type

universal_UNK_condition: Required evidence is not present anywhere in the supplied input sections.

rubric_formats.full: 6-string array, anchors for scores 0..5. Item-specific phrases at every level. Used for Q100 items (~100).
rubric_formats.compact: 4-string array, item-specific anchors mapped internally to scores 0/2/4/5. Levels 1 and 3 are interpolations between adjacent anchors and chosen by the LLM only when evidence is between two anchored states. Used for non-Q100 items (~400).

full: Not addressed; absent despite being clearly relevant.
Mentioned with minimal or unclear methodology.
Well-addressed with explicit method and justification.
Exemplary — transparent, with sensitivity analyses or methodological innovation.

input_levels.3: Detailed methods, results section, or limitations needed
input_levels.4: Tables / figures / supplement / external resources needed

scoring_modes.rule: Deterministic regex/parser extraction. Cheap, reproducible. Used for n=, p-values, AUROC, CI presence, registry IDs, etc.
scoring_modes.llm: LLM evidence-first scoring with rubric anchors. Required for subjective items (novelty, balance, honesty).
scoring_modes.hybrid: Rule extracts candidate evidence string(s); LLM applies rubric to it. Cheaper and more consistent than pure LLM.
scoring_modes.external: Requires an external database (PubMed/OpenAlex/journal directory) lookup beyond the manuscript text. E.g., 'guideline gap relevance' compared against current society guidelines.

reporting_guidelines.ROBINS-I: Risk of bias in non-randomized studies of interventions
reporting_guidelines.MI-CLAIM: Minimum information for clinical AI modeling

relation_kinds.canonical: This item is the canonical scoring of the concept; other items referring to the same concept should defer to this one in aggregation.
relation_kinds.subtype: This item is a domain-specific specialization of a canonical item. Both can be scored but downstream aggregation should down-weight the subtype to avoid double-counting.
relation_kinds.narrower: This item is a narrower aspect of a parent canonical item.
relation_kinds.broader: This item is a broader version that subsumes another item.

weights.rationale: Domain weights reflect predicted impact on citation/journal-tier in held-out 2023 corpus; will be re-estimated empirically once FateCore-v0.2 is trained. STATS/DESIGN/RELEV/EXTV/NOVEL weighted highest; REPRT/FIGS weighted lowest because their signal in citations is well-known to be weaker.

article_type_normalization.rule: Final FateCore score is computed AFTER article-type-specific normalization. Within each article_type, the scored set of applicable items has its own mean and SD baseline. A retrospective cohort is therefore not compared to RCTs on the absolute Q500 sum, only against other retrospective cohorts in the same domain.

field_semantics.name: Short human-readable label (≤6 words)
field_semantics.rubric: Array of 4 strings (compact) or 6 strings (full) — item-specific anchors
field_semantics.types: Array of article_types where this applies, or '*' for all
field_semantics.NA: Short condition string that makes this item NA
field_semantics.evidence: Array of short keywords or phrases describing what must be found in the manuscript to score >0
field_semantics.guideline: Array of reporting_guideline keys whose item this maps to
field_semantics.weight: Optional float — overrides default (1.0) for downstream aggregation
field_semantics.Q100: Boolean. true ⇒ item is in the abstract-only Q100 subset and has a full 6-anchor rubric
field_semantics.relation: Object {of: id, kind: relation_kind} — relates this item to a canonical one

extraction_output_schema.description: Per-item result stored after the server scores a manuscript with Q500.

fields.rationale_short: 1-sentence justification of the score against the rubric
fields.rubric_version: Rubric schema version used (matches this file's version)

extraction_prompt_outline.purpose: Reference outline for the system prompt used in llm/hybrid mode. Live prompt lives in src/lib/extractionPrompt.ts on the server.
steps: 2. Search for evidence matching the item's `evidence` keywords.
3. If no evidence is found anywhere in supplied input → emit UNK with confidence < 0.4.
4. If the article type is not in `types` (and no '*') → emit NA.
5. Otherwise quote the most relevant evidence span (≤30 words).
6. Identify the rubric anchor that best matches the evidence.
7. Emit score = anchor index, confidence based on quality of evidence match.
8. Write a 1-sentence rationale_short referencing the rubric anchor.
